paper.title: Lost Marie Curies: Parental Impact on the Probability of Becoming an Inventor
paper.code_data_availability: Supplemental Material: Data files and the online appendix are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2022.4432. …

registers.name_in_paper: Statistics Denmark registry data for the resident population of Denmark
registers.years: birth cohorts 1966-1985, with family information measured in the year the individual turned 15 and residence recorded at age 19
registers.role: sample frame, outcomes (educational trajectories), treatment (parental background), controls, linkage

registers.name_in_paper: PATSTAT, a database of the European Patent Office (EPO)
registers.role: treatment and outcome: identification of inventors
variables_mentioned: inventor name and private address on EP patent applications

linkages: EP patent applications with at least one Danish resident inventor are matched to Statistics Denmark registry data on disambiguated inventor name and private address; where no match is found, Statistics Denmark searches by name among the employees of the Danish patent assignee(s). 87% of inventors with a Danish address are matched.
Children are linked to their legal mother and legal father, so that parental education, parental income and parental inventorship can be attached to the focal individual.
Siblings are identified as full siblings, i.e. siblings who have the same legal parents, and ordered by birth to define first-born and second-born.

sample.universe: All individuals born in Denmark between 1966 and 1985 and listed as residents in the government registry at age 19 (gross population 1,351,394 individuals)
sample.unit_of_observation: individual (one observation per person; no panel dimension)
selection_rules: Born in Denmark 1966-1985 and resident in the government registry at age 19 (1,351,394 individuals)
Complete information on the variables described in Table 1, Panel A: 1,191,849 individuals (88% of the gross population), referred to as the full population
Individuals who did not live with either of their legal parents at age 15 are excluded (2.3% of the gross population; 31,136 individuals)
23 matched inventors who were supposedly less than 20 years old at their first patent application are treated as likely mismatches and omitted

For the sibling experiment: first-borns only, with a full sibling (same legal parents) born within four years (eight years in Table 4, Panel B); twins and siblings separated by less than nine months excluded; single-child families excluded
For the stepwise regressions: subsamples of high school completers, of tertiary education (BSc+) completers, and of STEM tertiary education (BSc+) completers
sample.n_observations: 1,191,849 individuals in the full population (579,676 women; 612,173 men); 122,709 first-born women and 131,087 first-born men with a second-born sibling within four years

construction_notes: Inventorship equals one if an individual is listed as an inventor with a DK country code on at least one EP application in the period 1978 (the founding year of the EPO) to 2015, and zero otherwise; 4,626 inventors are identified in the full population, an incidence rate of about four inventors per thousand.
Family-related variables (income, municipality of residence, living arrangement) are extracted for the year in which the person turned 15.
Real disposable income is family disposable income in real 2000 Danish Kroner, logged.

GPA is the sum of all grades received divided by the number of classes taken in high school, measured on a 0-13 scale with 6 the passing grade; it is available for almost all math- and language-track students but only 43% of technical and 63% of 'Other' high school students.

High school completers are divided into four tracks: math, language, tech and other (business, higher preparatory, international baccalaureate); Math-tech high-school track equals one for the math or tech track.
STEM BSc+ equals one for tertiary education completed in science, engineering, or food and agricultural sciences.
Tertiary education means a university bachelor's degree or higher (MSc or PhD) or a professional bachelor's degree.
All regressions include municipality-of-residence-at-age-15 dummies (reference: Copenhagen) and year-of-birth dummies (reference year 1976).
The 1985 cohort reached age 30 in 2015, the last year of the patent sample; Table 4, Panel D restricts to the 1966-1975 cohorts, observed to at least age 40.

claims.statement: Among the full population of women, Lived with single mother has no statistically significant association with being an inventor (-0.0001, standard error 0.0001).
